written.myAnswer: A mole is an amount of substance containing 6.022 × 10²³ specified entities; Avogadro’s number is the numerical value 6.022 × 10²³.
Avogadro’s number links the huge numbers of atoms or molecules in a sample to measurable amounts of substance and mass, allowing chemists to calculate quantities in reactions.
Avogadro’s number is 6.022 × 10²³, the number of specified entities in one mole. A mole is the amount of substance containing that number of entities.
